name: Palliative and hospice care
summary: How expat families navigate palliative medicine and hospice services in Singapore for serious illness symptom control, home hospice, and end-of-life planning — including pass, housing, and cross-border family logistics.
body:
Palliative care is specialist symptom control and support for serious illness — not only “last days.” It can run alongside oncology, cardiology, or neurology treatment. Hospice services add home, day, or inpatient end-of-life settings when goals shift.

## What to expect
- Pain, breathlessness, nausea, and delirium management
- Goals-of-care and Advance Care Planning conversations
- Home hospice nursing visits and caregiver coaching
- Respite and inpatient hospice when home care collapses
- Psychosocial and bereavement support

Oncology and hospital palliative teams often introduce services; community hospices (e.g. well-known voluntary welfare organisations) extend care at home. Ask for early referral rather than crisis-only contact.

## Expat-specific friction
Employment Pass households may have limited local family caregivers. Helper training, condo access for hospice nurses, and landlord sensitivity matter. Overseas relatives flying in need clear medical summaries and visitation norms. Funeral/repatriation planning can run in parallel — see that service guide when remains logistics become relevant.

## Costs and coverage
Subsidy frameworks differ for citizens/PRs vs foreigners. Private insurance may cover limited palliative inpatient days — read cancer and chronic-illness riders carefully. Voluntary hospices explain fees upfront; do not assume “hospice = free” for EP holders.

## How to choose
Prefer teams that coordinate with your oncologist/hospitalist, offer 24/7 phone advice, and document preferred place of death realistically. Language-matched social workers help when the patient is not English-dominant. Avoid anyone pushing unproven cures at the palliative transition.

## Practical tip
Keep a one-page med list, allergy list, and decision-maker contacts on the fridge for night visits. Nominate a local logistics lead even if financial decisions sit with overseas siblings.
